$comment: The single place where this package knows pi's tool names.
Layer bodies reference capabilities as {{delegate}}, {{search}}, ... and never
name a tool directly — a test enforces that. When pi renames or drops a tool,
edit this file; the four layer bodies stay untouched.
required=true : a layer listing this capability in `requires-capabilities` is
skipped entirely when the tool is absent.
required=false: the tool is merely mentioned; when absent, `absent` is
substituted so no dead tool name survives into the prompt.
Deliberately excluded: read / grep / write / edit. They are pi's most primitive
tools (least likely to be renamed) and they are ordinary English words, so
placeholder-ing them would make the prose unreadable and the bare-name test useless.

delegate_parallel.absent: the dispatch tool, once per task

agents.name: explore
agents.use: read-only investigation; sweeps the repo and returns compressed findings with file:line evidence. The default first dispatch whenever you cannot yet name the files a change touches — it runs the cheap retrieval tier precisely so the implementer does not.

agents.name: plan
agents.use: read-only; turns a goal into a numbered list of dispatchable steps. Reach for it when the decomposition itself depends on code nobody has read yet.

agents.name: general-purpose
agents.use: the only agent that edits files. Implements one brief and runs its verify.

agents.name: reviewer
agents.use: read-only judgement machines cannot make: design quality, off-target work, security risk, arbitrating workers that contradict each other.

agents.name: operator
agents.use: compatibility-only desktop worker. When computer_task is available, never dispatch operator directly: give computer_task the natural-language goal and let its private Leader supervise isolated workers and return one final report.

agents.name: secretary
agents.use: optional closeout audit: reconciles worktrees, branches and leftover artifacts. Advisory, and never owns the completion decision.
